task:
COLONY PLANNER S4 FOLLOW-UP ON THE SAME BRANCH (plan/s4-page): MAKE THE /plan PAGE COMPACT, "AT A GLANCE" LIKE RAVEN COLONIAL'S SYSTEM VIEW. LAYOUT/CSS/MARKUP ONLY IN apps/web/src/lib/features/plan/ AND ITS TESTS. NO BEHAVIOUR, DATA, STORAGE OR API CHANGES.

Why: the owner's main feedback on the design was that the planner must show more at a glance. A visual check of this branch with the owner's real 82-site plan for a 42-body system (1600×1000 viewport) found the page 18,100 px tall and the System pane alone 10,700 px: every body takes about 190 px (name row, a row of long text badges, a row of large slot boxes) and every build-order step about 215 px (separate rows for status, chips, three buttons and an "Edit" disclosure). Everything works; it is just far too spread out.

Targets at 1600×1000 with that plan (42 bodies, 2 belts, 82 sites): System pane content ≤ 2,600 px; each build-order step ≤ 64 px when its edit panel is closed; nothing overlaps; phone width (390 px) still has no horizontal scroll.

System pane:
1. One line per body or belt (about 30–34 px): connector line, disc (16–28 px, radius-scaled as now), short name, feature MARKERS, the two slot boxes, then the "+" button at the end. Replace the long text badges ("Volcanism: Major Silicate Vapour Geysers", "Atmosphere: Hot thick Argon-rich", "Landable", "Rings", "Metal Rich") with short markers (for example ⛰ landable, ◎ rings, G2 geological, B1 biological, V volcanism, A atmosphere, T terraformable; belts: ring type initial or a small text such as "Metal-rich") whose full text is in `title` and in the accessible name. Markers must not be colour-only.
2. Slot boxes become small inline chips on the same line, e.g. "◌ 1/2" (orbital) and "◍ 0/3" (surface), still buttons that open the existing slot editor, still showing "?" for unknown, "–" for not landable, and the over-capacity highlight. Keep their accessible names ("Orbital slots: 1 used of 2 …").
3. Site tiles stay as they are in content but become single-line chips (about 24 px) that wrap under their body with a small indent; remove extra vertical padding/borders between bodies (rely on the connector lines and a 2–4 px gap).
4. The pane scrolls inside itself on wide screens (max-height about calc(100vh − header), overflow auto) so the Summary stays in view; on phones it does not scroll internally.

Build order pane:
5. Each step on at most two lines when closed. Line 1: index circle, site name, "Primary Port" label when first, muted "facility · orbital/surface · body", result chip (icon + word) at the right. Line 2: status, cost and earn chips, "port #n" when present, running "After" totals, then icon buttons Move up ↑ and Move down ↓ (keep their accessible names "Move up"/"Move down" and disabled rules), a "Why?" button, and a small "Edit" button that opens the existing edit panel below the step. The Primary Port protection sentence (RB-0008) appears only inside the opened edit panel and as the disabled buttons' title, not as a paragraph on the step.
6. The pane scrolls inside itself on wide screens like the System pane.

Summary pane: make it `position: sticky` within the grid on wide screens so it stays visible while the other two panes scroll.

Glyph fix: the "building" status glyph (◐) falls back to a different glyph in the app font. Use small inline SVG (or CSS) icons for complete / building / planned / demolished and for OK / Blocked / Needs info, with the word kept in the accessible name.

Keep every existing behaviour, accessible name, keyboard path, live-region announcement and test passing (update snapshot-like assertions only where markup moved). Keep the Cypress spec working (adjust selectors only if needed, never weaken its assertions). Add one Vitest/component test that renders a 40-body, 80-site fixture and asserts each body row and each closed step render on a single compact row (for example via the row container having no line-wrapping child blocks, or via class names you introduce for compact rows) — whatever is robust in jsdom.

VALIDATION: in apps/web: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm test` (report counts), `pnpm build`. SUMMARY: the files changed and what each layout change was.
